cards.headline: The closing instrumental that Rolling Stone tied to Lost in Translation
cards.snippet: In February 2004, Rob Sheffield reviewed Air's album Talkie Walkie for Rolling Stone. He noted that its closing instrumental, "Alone in Kyoto," had already appeared memorably in Sofia Coppola's film Lost in Translation. He went further and called the album basically the musical equivalent of that film. In his words, it is a slow-motion romance where nothing much happens, yet even the quiet moments send out emotional ripples that seem to go on forever.

cards.headline: Pitchfork heard a Japanese imperial garden suite
cards.snippet: In a January 2004 review of Air's Talkie Walkie, Pitchfork described "Alone in Kyoto" as a Japanese imperial garden suite. The critic placed it in the album's second half, alongside "Surfin' on a Rocket," "Alpha Beta Gaga" and "Biological." He said those tracks rework Brian Wilson's surfing symphonies through the Berlin-era flipsides of Bowie and Eno. The review also credited producer Nigel Godrich's minimal, detailed recording for the album's chilling resonance.

cards.headline: A 15-year promise kept
cards.snippet: When I was a teenager during my first trip ever in Prague, I swore to myself I would listen to this in Kyoto one day. Its nighttime in Kyoto 15 years later, and I fulfilled the promise.

replies.author: @logycaa
replies.text: So cool. I hope to fulfill something very similar one day: return to Japan, this time in Hokkaido, and listen to Shingo Nakamura's "Sapporo" while walking in the town
